shell.banner: Concept demonstration • Fictional client and financing terms • Not connected to BDC.
shell.resetBody: This clears the local demo events, any drafted or created demo requests, survey responses, the Clair conversation and “Mark as reviewed”. The notice itself does not change.
shell.footerData: This single file contains fictional data only. No information you enter leaves this browser, except when you choose to open an external BDC link. The accessibility widget is the one online service this page loads automatically.
aboutBody: Concept prototype of an interactive financing notice. Camille Roy, Atelier Boréal Inc., the loan and all amounts are fictional. Nothing here is a BDC offer, agreement, policy or system.
Clair is a proposed demo name. In this file it answers only from this sample notice using local rules; there is no live AI connection.
The narration was generated before distribution with ElevenLabs text-to-speech and is embedded in this file. Playback never contacts ElevenLabs.
Demo requests, survey answers and “Mark as reviewed” stay in this browser tab and are cleared when you reset or close it.

summary.extra-interest: Additional interest over the remaining schedule

chart.payments: Payment comparison chart, November to April

clauses.cost: 7. Effect on interest and total payments

principal.definition: The amount borrowed that remains to be repaid, excluding interest.

interest.definition: The cost of borrowing, calculated using the balance and the applicable rate.

postponement.definition: Delaying principal payments for a set period. Interest may still be payable during that time.

instalment.definition: A scheduled payment under the financing arrangement.

maturity.definition: The date the remaining loan balance is scheduled to be fully repaid.

outstanding.definition: Principal still owing at the relevant date.

fixedRate.definition: A rate that does not change during the specified fixed-rate period.

cashFlow.definition: Money coming into and going out of the business.

amortisation.definition: Repayment of principal over a schedule.

capitalisedInterest.definition: Interest added to the amount owing. This does not occur in this demonstration.

overview.greeting: Hello, {name}. Let’s walk through your financing update.
overview.title: Your principal payments are postponed for three months.
overview.intro: In this fictional example, the temporary [[postponement|principal postponement]] requested for {company} has been approved and the amendment is complete. Here is what it means for your payments, and what stays the same.

illustration.caption: Illustration of a manufacturing workshop. Not a photograph of the recipient or BDC staff.

summary.title: Your update at a glance
summary.intro: Each card leads to the month-by-month detail behind the figure.

next-payment.label: Next payment
next-payment.note: Interest only. No principal is due this month.

resume.label: Principal payments resume
resume.note: First payment after the postponement: {total} ({principal} principal + {interest} interest).

beside.title: Keep in mind
beside.maturityText: Your final payment moves from {from} to {to}.
beside.owingText: The {amount} of postponed principal remains owing. This is temporary cash-flow relief, not a reduction in what you owe.

todo.title: What you need to do
todo.step1Text: Check the revised dates and amounts, starting with the payment due {date}.
todo.step2Text: Plan for interest-only payments of {interest} from {from} to {to}, then a payment of {resumed} on {resumeDate}, when principal payments resume.
todo.noAcceptance: No acceptance is required through this notice. The amendment is already approved and complete.
todo.markHint: Optional. Keeps a note in this browser tab only.
todo.reviewedStatus: Marked as reviewed in this demo. This is a local note only — not acceptance, consent or proof of understanding.

same.title: What stays the same
same.intro: The postponement changes when principal is repaid. These terms do not change.

media.unavailableText: The explanation player is not included in this build. The same information is on this page and in “What changed”.
